title: Meeting Mamie Smith through Perry Bradford
summary: Bradford heard him practicing behind his house, took him to meet Mamie Smith, and he recorded and then toured with her five-piece band.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: It was just a record, two sides. Seventy-five cents. Yeah. Speaking about recording, the next session I did was with Mamie Smith and the way Peery Bradford heard me -- he was her manager then and also the writer of those tunes -- I lived at 130th Street and Peery lived directly behind me on 129th Street and he had heard me practicing on my house and he said, 'Hey, clarinet player,' I didn't know him, he didn't know

me. He said, "You play clarinet, huh?" I said, "Yeah, I try to." "How'd you like to make some records?" I said, "Fine." "Come on over my house," so I strapped my clarinet case on my back and climbed over the back fence and went through his kitchen upstairs and there was Mamie Smith sitting there.
That's when you met Mamie Smith.
That's when I -- yeah. Mamie Smith -- and from then on I have recorded, and after making records with her the following summer I went on the road with her.
That was five-piece -- five-piece band. Trumpet, trombone, clarinet, piano, drums.
